name: GhostBSD
summary: A user-friendly, desktop-oriented BSD operating system built upon FreeBSD, providing an out-of-the-box MATE graphical environment, automated OpenZFS installation with boot environments, and dedicated graphical management tools.

content.introduction: GhostBSD is an open-source, desktop-oriented Unix-like operating system founded in 2010 by Eric Turgeon. Designed to combine the stability, security, and performance of the FreeBSD operating system with an accessible, modern desktop experience, GhostBSD eliminates the manual configuration traditionally required to set up a graphical BSD workstation.
content.what_is_it: GhostBSD is a turnkey, pre-configured operating system delivering a fully functional graphical desktop environment based on FreeBSD RELEASE branches. It features the MATE desktop environment by default (with community XFCE editions), an intuitive graphical installer, custom system administration utilities, and pre-packaged graphics drivers for AMD, Intel, and Nvidia hardware.
content.origin_and_freebsd_foundation: Originating in 2010 as a project aimed at simplifying desktop FreeBSD deployment, GhostBSD initially drew upon FreeBSD development branches before aligning with TrueOS infrastructure, and subsequently transitioning to track upstream FreeBSD RELEASE directly. Starting with release 25.01-R14.2p1, GhostBSD adopted a transparent versioning scheme tied directly to the underlying FreeBSD release patchsets, ensuring superior operational predictability. Initiated by Canadian developer Eric Turgeon, GhostBSD originally used FreeBSD release branches before transitioning its underlying build infrastructure to FreeBSD STABLE to ensure timely desktop hardware driver backports.
content.desktop_environment_and_tooling: GhostBSD delivers a complete, polished graphical desktop experience built around a tailored MATE desktop environment, complemented by community editions featuring XFCE. It integrates the LightDM display manager and a custom suite of administrative utilities engineered in Python and GTK. Chief among these is Networkmgr, a system tray applet that provides graphical Wi-Fi (WPA2/WPA3) and Ethernet network configuration without requiring users to manually configure `/etc/wpa_supplicant.conf` or `rc.conf`. For software administration, GhostBSD includes Software Station, a graphical front-end for browsing, installing, and updating desktop applications, and Update Station, which streamlines system upgrades while insulating end users from underlying command-line package management complexities.
content.storage_and_boot_environments: GhostBSD adopts OpenZFS as its mandatory root file system, automated through its graphical installer, GBI (GhostBSD Installer). The installer partitions storage drives and provisions ZFS storage pools (zpools) with optimal dataset alignments and compression (lz4) enabled by default. Because OpenZFS underpins the base operating system, GhostBSD fully leverages ZFS Boot Environments (`bectl` and `beadm`). Prior to executing system or kernel updates via Update Station, the operating system automatically captures an atomic snapshot of the active root dataset and provisions a new boot environment. If an update encounters incompatible hardware drivers or package regressions, users can easily roll back to the previously functional system snapshot directly from the FreeBSD boot loader menu at startup.
content.package_management_and_releases: Rather than pointing directly to bleeding-edge FreeBSD upstream package repositories, GhostBSD maintains its own dedicated binary package repositories. These repositories are compiled using dedicated Poudriere build servers tracking FreeBSD STABLE, applying custom desktop patches and stabilizing package versions to prevent desktop breakage common in rolling development ports. GhostBSD uses the standard FreeBSD `pkg` utility under the hood, ensuring binary compatibility with the extensive FreeBSD software ecosystem. The project follows a continuous quarterly release rhythm, issuing bootable live ISO images with out-of-the-box hardware detection for Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA graphics hardware.
content.hardware_target_and_installation_media: GhostBSD targets 64-bit x86 (amd64) exclusively. The project publishes two images for the current 26.1-R15.0p2 release, one with MATE and one with XFCE, and states minimum requirements of a 64-bit processor, 8 GB of RAM, 15 GB of free storage and a network connection. Installation media are ISO images written to a USB stick with dd on FreeBSD, Linux or macOS, or with Rufus on Windows. The graphical installer configures networking, keyboard layout and full-disk ZFS encryption during setup.
content.package_sources_and_update_tools: Beyond the FreeBSD base system, GhostBSD maintains its own repositories of prebuilt packages, synchronised periodically with the FreeBSD ports collection and served through `pkg`, with desktop-specific additions such as preconfigured NVIDIA drivers, the Slick LightDM greeter and multimedia codecs. Two graphical tools drive maintenance: Update Station, which creates a bootable ZFS boot environment through `pybectl` before applying a system upgrade, and Backup Station, which manages boot environments from the desktop.
advantages: Out-of-the-box desktop BSD experience with zero manual command-line configuration required
Native OpenZFS integration with automated boot environment snapshots before system upgrades
Dedicated graphical administration suite including NetworkMgr, Update Station, and Software Station
Curated binary package repositories pre-configured with proprietary graphics drivers and codecs
Rock-solid FreeBSD RELEASE foundation providing broad BSD software ecosystem compatibility
disadvantages: Strictly limited to 64-bit x86_64 hardware, with no official ARM64 or 32-bit images
Wireless device compatibility and consumer peripheral support lag behind mainstream desktop Linux
Smaller application catalog compared to major Linux distributions, requiring Linuxulator for specific binaries
who_is_it_for: Users seeking an accessible, daily-driver desktop powered by the FreeBSD kernel and OpenZFS
Developers, systems administrators, and Unix enthusiasts learning BSD in a graphical environment
Users requiring a resilient workstation with instant ZFS snapshot rollback capabilities
who_is_it_not_for: Gamers expecting comprehensive out-of-the-box Proton, Steam Anti-Cheat, and cutting-edge GPU support
Users deploying lightweight operating systems on ARM evaluation boards, Raspberry Pi, or 32-bit machines
content.verdict: GhostBSD combines a FreeBSD RELEASE base with a MATE desktop, graphical administration tools, and automated OpenZFS boot environments. It provides a FreeBSD-based desktop system preconfigured with these tools.
